name: Catalonia
summary: The Senyera: four red stripes on gold. One of the oldest flags in Europe still in use, it was the royal sign of the Counts of Barcelona and the Crown of Aragon.
origin: The red and gold stripes appear on the seals of the Counts of Barcelona from the 12th century. A legend says Wilfred the Hairy's bloody fingers drew the stripes on a gold shield; this is a later invention. The Senyera became official in the 1979 Statute of Autonomy.
facts: Independence supporters fly the Estelada, which adds a star in a triangle.
The legend of Wilfred the Hairy was invented centuries after his death.
clues: Four red stripes on gold, nothing else.
By legend its stripes were drawn in blood by a count's fingers.
One of the oldest flags in Europe still in use.
